noAnchorGaps.concept: Tenkan (blue) and Kijun (yellow) lines identified by name
noAnchorGaps.quote: The blue line is the Tenkan, the yellow is the Kijun
noAnchorGaps.why: move ichimoku exposes only pullback(pt) and aboveCloud(pt); no anchor sits on the Tenkan or Kijun line itself, so they cannot be labelled. The move already renders them in blue/yellow.

noAnchorGaps.concept: Tenkan crosses above the Kijun = bullish momentum signal
noAnchorGaps.quote: When the fast Tenkan crosses above the slower Kijun, that's a bullish momentum signal
noAnchorGaps.why: move ichimoku exposes no anchor at the Tenkan/Kijun crossover point (only pullback and aboveCloud), so the cross cannot be marked without inventing an anchor.

noAnchorGaps.concept: The Kumo cloud as a thick zone of support/resistance
noAnchorGaps.quote: the cloud itself is a thick zone of support or resistance — the thicker it is, the stronger it holds
noAnchorGaps.why: move ichimoku exposes no (L) level anchor at all (only point anchors pullback and aboveCloud), so a labelled S/R zone band on the cloud cannot be attached. The cloud is already drawn by the move.

notes: Both CHART beats are already complete and correct. cloud: note@aboveCloud 'price above a green cloud = bullish' (valid pt anchor, matches 'price is trading above the cloud, and the cloud is green'). signals: note@pullback 'Kijun holds as support' (valid pt anchor, matches 'pullbacks find it and bounce'); accumulates the aboveCloud note from the same-chart cloud beat. The ichimoku move exposes ONLY pullback(pt) and aboveCloud(pt) — zero level anchors — so the Tenkan/Kijun line labels, the Tenkan/Kijun cross marker, and the cloud S/R zone are all genuinely undrawable and correctly recorded as noAnchorGaps. The Tenkan/Kijun/Kumo are rendered by the move itself, so naming them adds no gap. Auditor's proposal upheld in full; no adds, no fixes.
